pages.text: X-rays scattered by successive planes of atoms reinforce only where the extra path between planes is a whole number of wavelengths: nλ = 2d·sin θ. A copper anode gives its Kα line, λ = 1.5406 Å - but only when the tube voltage can knock out a K-shell electron, above 8.98 kV. The count rate grows with the current and steeply with the overvoltage.
$(thing)Set$(): Tube voltage V, Tube current I, Detector angle 2θ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Thermal drift of the goniometer: the angle wanders by ±0.05°·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Below copper's K-edge: no Kα line; The anode is melting (above 2.2 kW).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More X-rays, a faster exposure.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Bragg angle θ: θ = 2θ/2$(br)Spacing that reflects: d = λ/(2 sin θ)$(br)Mismatch: |d − d_lattice|/d_lattice$(br)Anode power: P = V·I$(br)Count rate: N ∝ I·(V − V_K)^1.6
